summary: Marco Walther is a scholar of Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich (attested 2017), where he was supervised by Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and also studied under Khenpo Dondrup Namgyal.

Marcus Bingenheimer is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Würzburg under Norbert Klaes and Huinan Yang. He held posts at Dharma Drum Institute, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Temple University.

Marek Mejor (1950–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a junior research fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and was a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under the supervision of Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil (1952–2011) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Sheffield from 1972 to 1976 and later held an academic post there from approximately 1981 to 2011.

Margaret Dornish is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California. She served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).
Margaret Gouin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret J. Pearson is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She pursued doctoral studies at the University of Washington under Hellmut Wilhelm and Burton Watson, and was a Visiting Fellow at Clare Hall, Cambridge, in 1997.

Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at Barnard and Columbia under Franz Boas. She held posts at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, Fordham University, and the University of Rhode Island, and founded NYU (1965) and Fordham (1968).

Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religion and history. She earned her PhD from the Graduate Theological Union and held posts at Harvard Divinity School, Graduate Theological Union as dean, and served as president of the American Academy of Religion.

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower (attested 2016) and completed postdoctoral work mentored by Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Kleibel is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Karin Preisendanz and completed her master's degree under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010).

Margarita Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya (1933–2021) was an Indology and Central Asian specialist educated at St. Petersburg University. She spent decades at the Institute of Oriental Studies and curated Central Asian manuscripts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Maria Heim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, later serving as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College.

Marian Ury (1932–1995) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1953, and served as a professor at the University of California, Davis, from 1969 to 1995.

Marianne Pieper is a sociologist who studied at the University of Hamburg and completed her habilitation at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. She held posts at the University of Kassel and served as a sociology professor at Hamburg.

Marianne Winder (1918–2001) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS. She worked at the University of Nottingham, University of London, and as a curator and consultant at the Wellcome Institute.
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Pennsylvania under the instruction of Sengaku Mayeda.

Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 2006 under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman, also studying with Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley.

Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He held academic posts at Hampshire College and Rollins College.
